question: A science class started an experiment with 15 seedlings, while a dozen extra pots sat unused on a shelf nearby. The seedlings were multiplied across 7 identical trays, each holding that same amount, for the greenhouse. A pest problem killed 74 seedlings. A late addition brought 49 more seedlings into the count. A second greenhouse order required the total to grow to 9 times its size. A final donation added 40 more seedlings. How many seedlings were there after the donation?

A print shop began the day with 16 flyers, multiplied across 7 identical print runs, each producing that same amount, for a campaign. A second campaign made that total grow to 9 times its size. Unrelated to flyers, a nearby office ordered 500 reams of paper that same day. A third campaign made the total grow to 4 times its size. Since the shop counts flyers individually but the invoice bills by the ream, the manager always converted the numbers. A final citywide order required the total to grow to 3 times its size. How many flyers were needed for the citywide order?

A construction site started the morning with 212 bricks, multiplied across 4 identical pallets, each holding that same amount, for a wall project. A delivery added 60 more bricks, and a second delivery added 36 more bricks. A second wall project required the total to grow to 8 times its size. Since the crew measures bricks by count but the supplier invoices by weight, the foreman kept a conversion sheet. A third project made the total grow to 2 times its size. A final addition brought 32 more bricks. How many bricks were on site after that addition?

A comic book shop began the morning with 47 comics on the new-release shelf. By afternoon, 3 comics were damaged and pulled from the shelf. A convention order required the remaining stock to grow to 4 times its size. A shipping recall then removed 114 comics found to be misprinted. A late donation added 36 more comics. How many comics were on the shelf after that donation?

A car wash began the day with 176 dollars earned, multiplied across 7 identical stations, each earning that same amount, for the week's total. A tip jar added 8 more dollars. Unrelated to the car wash, a nearby gas station sold 200 gallons of fuel that same day. A bonus added 11 more dollars. Since the shop records earnings in dollars but the franchise report lists cents, the manager always converted the numbers. A matching program made the total grow to 4 times its size. How much money did the car wash have after that program?

Two farmers, Rosalind and Thaddeus, tracked corn crates, and Thaddeus's harvest always trailed hers. Rosalind's morning harvest was multiplied across 3 identical fields, each yielding 161 crates, combined into one total. By afternoon, a second harvest made that total grow to 6 times its size. That evening, 510 crates were sold to a regional buyer. Overnight, a late gift added 30 more crates. How many crates did Rosalind have by the next morning?

Two hikers, Balthazar and Ottilie, tracked trail snacks, and Balthazar always packed less than she did, a dozen bars short from the very start. Ottilie began the morning with 186 granola bars. By midmorning, 170 bars were given to a scout troop they passed. In the afternoon, a friend gave her 17 more bars. That evening, a second friend gave her 14 more bars. Overnight, a cousin added 54 more bars. Right before dawn, 1 bar was lost to a curious raccoon. How many granola bars did Ottilie have by dawn?

Jason had 240 cents saved in his piggy bank, an amount his older sister liked to point out was just under two and a half dollars. One afternoon he split the coins evenly with his younger brother so each of them would have spending money for the fair. After buying a sticker for 5 cents at the entrance booth, he wandered over to a coin-multiplier game that promised to turn every cent into eight cents, and he walked away with eight times what he'd fed into the machine. His grandmother then gave him 55 cents for helping weed her garden that morning, and his aunt slipped him another 44 cents as a birthday treat. How many cents did Jason have in the end?

Every morning, Marcus opens his food truck's cash drawer with exactly $118 left over from the day before. By mid-morning he had taken in $80 from the breakfast crowd, even though a dozen of his regular customers paid with cards instead of cash. In the early afternoon he had to pay a produce supplier $157 for a delivery, a round trip that took 120 minutes, a full two hours, through downtown traffic. That same afternoon, a promotional partner matched whatever was left in the drawer four times over as part of a grand-opening event. By evening, Marcus split that afternoon total evenly four ways among his four business partners, keeping only his own share in the drawer. He then added $67 from the dinner rush, but had to pay out $103 to cover a broken generator. How much money was left in the drawer at closing?

Nina counted $45 in her wallet, quite a bit more than the $10 her friend Priya had brought along, and tucked a dozen stickers into her pocket just for fun. At the farmers market she sold a hand-painted birdhouse and earned $62. She then spent $60 on a new set of paintbrushes and $5 on a lemonade to cool off. Later she paid her younger cousin $29 for helping carry supplies back to the car, and finally gave $12 to the market's donation jar for local schools. How much money did Nina have left?

On Monday morning, a hardware store had 228 hammers in stock, though 90 of them were still shrink-wrapped from a shipment nobody had logged yet. By midday, a contractor bought 168 hammers for a big framing job. In the afternoon a supplier dropped off 25 replacement hammers, and by evening a return truck brought back another 50 that customers had exchanged. That night, the store tripled its hammer stock by unpacking cases from the back room, ending with three times as many hammers as it had before the unpacking. How many hammers did the store have after unpacking the cases?

Camila had 168 minutes of phone data left at the start of the month, just under three hours as her plan summary put it. She earned 38 bonus minutes for referring a friend, then used up 205 minutes during a long weekend of video calls with family. Her provider credited her 36 minutes back after a service outage, and separately mailed her a coupon for a dozen free stickers that had nothing to do with her data plan. Finally, she redeemed a survey reward worth 28 minutes. How many minutes did Camila have left?

A moving company's truck started the day loaded with 209 boxes. At the first stop the crew picked up 19 more boxes, and at the second stop they added 44 boxes, even as the dispatch radio mentioned an unrelated truck across town carrying 1,200 boxes. At the third stop, they delivered 205 boxes to a client's new office. Back at the depot, seven identical truckloads arrived at the same time, so the loading dock ended up holding eight times as many boxes as this one truck alone had carried. A late vendor delivery then added 63 more boxes, and 447 boxes went out on the evening shipment to local stores. How many boxes were left at the depot?

On the morning of the science fair, Priya's petri dish held 89 bacteria cells, according to her 9 a.m. count, just three hours, or 180 minutes, before the noon judging. A contamination event that morning killed off 38 of the cells. Over the next few hours, the surviving colony multiplied sevenfold as it fed on the agar's nutrients. By afternoon, a warmer incubator setting caused the colony to multiply another fivefold. Priya then introduced 41 cells from a backup sample she'd been growing separately. By evening, a final growth spurt multiplied the whole colony sixfold before the judges scored it. How many bacteria cells were in the dish by evening?

A packing house's bin held 240 apples at the start of the morning, though the manager mentioned a completely unrelated order of 10,000 apples destined for a different client entirely. Workers picked 20 more apples and tossed them into the same bin. To fill a large export order, the crew multiplied the bin's contents ninefold by matching every apple with eight more from cold storage. That export batch was then split evenly across five delivery trucks, and only the lead truck's load is tracked from here. The lead truck's apples were further divided evenly onto six pallets for the warehouse, and only one of those pallets continued to the final buyer. Finally, 23 apples from a late harvest were added to that pallet. How many apples were on the pallet after the late harvest was added?

Derek owned 217 trading cards, far more than his cousin Bianca's 15. At a swap meet he traded up and gained 67 more cards. A rare booster-box promotion then let him multiply his entire collection ninefold by redeeming a golden ticket. A second, even rarer promotion at a different booth multiplied his whole collection another fourfold. Later, he sold off 367 duplicate cards to a dealer to make room in his binder. How many cards did Derek have left after the sale?

At sunrise, a beekeeper counted 189 bees in a new hive, alongside a completely unrelated apiary a mile away that was said to hold a dozen hives of its own. By mid-morning, the queen's brood hatched, and the colony's population became four times what it had been at sunrise. In the afternoon, a spell of cold weather caused 215 bees to die off. Later that afternoon, a second wave of hatching multiplied the surviving colony sixfold. That evening, a swarm split off, taking 1,484 bees away to start a new hive elsewhere. Overnight, 27 bees returned after getting lost during the swarm. By the next morning, a pesticide drift in a nearby field killed off 572 more bees. How many bees remained in the original hive?

A theater had 129 seats reserved for a school trip, while a completely unrelated concert next door had booked 500 seats of its own. A dozen chaperones came along, though that number played no role in the seat count as 43 students had to cancel due to a scheduling conflict. Afterward, 36 more students from another class joined the trip. Then 92 seats were released back to the box office when a different school pulled out of a joint booking. Finally, 30 walk-up students joined, and 78 more students from a nearby school added their names to the trip. How many students ended up going on the trip?

Maria's savings account held 201 dollars, or 20,100 cents as the bank teller once pointed out. She deposited 42 dollars from her paycheck, along with a loyalty card now stamped a dozen times, which earned her no extra cash. A loyalty bonus then multiplied her balance sevenfold as a reward for years of banking with them. She split that reward evenly three ways with her two siblings, keeping only her own third. Finally, she paid 542 dollars toward a new laptop. How much money did Maria have left in her account?

Jake had 214 baseball cards, more than his friend Marcus's 90. A trading event doubled his entire collection when he matched every card with an identical one from a bulk lot. He then found 4 more cards under his bed. He split the collection evenly among six binders, keeping only one binder's worth. That binder was further divided evenly across four subject dividers, and he kept only the modern-era divider's cards. Finally, he bought 19 more modern-era cards at a shop. How many cards were in that divider afterward?

In the morning, Aisha had 112 pesos in her wallet, more than her cousin Bruno's 30. By midday she earned 43 pesos selling lemonade. In the afternoon she paid 124 pesos for a new umbrella. Later that afternoon a friend repaid her a 53-peso loan. By evening she spent 20 pesos on dinner and 57 pesos on a taxi ride home. Finally, she paid 1 peso in a small service fee. How many pesos did Aisha have left?

A charity box started the fundraiser with 100 dollars in it. Within the first hour, 91 dollars was withdrawn to buy raffle supplies. A local business then donated 40 dollars, and a second donor added 25 dollars. A matching-fund sponsor multiplied whatever was in the box fivefold at the end of the night. Organizers then paid 306 dollars for the venue rental. Finally, a latecomer dropped in 10 dollars. How much money was in the box at the end?

A comic book shop had 16 rare comics in a locked case, plus a dozen common comics on a nearby spinner rack that don't count toward this total. A collector sold the shop 29 more rare comics. A convention then let the shop multiply its rare stock fivefold through a bulk trade with another dealer. Afterward, 3 comics were found to be damaged and removed. A second trade multiplied the stock fivefold again, and a final wholesale deal multiplied it ninefold once more. How many rare comics did the shop end up with?

Wei had 162 minutes of video-call credit, or two hours and forty-two minutes as his phone app displayed it, more than his roommate Tom's 15 minutes. He split the credit evenly across six family group chats, and this story follows only one of those chats from here. That chat then received a 26-minute bonus from a promotion. A loyalty reward multiplied the chat's remaining minutes sevenfold. Finally, 243 minutes were used up during a long weekend of calls. How many minutes were left in that chat?

A beehive had 12 honeycomb frames at the start of spring, while a completely separate hive across the field held 200 frames of its own. The colony then multiplied its frame count sevenfold as new comb was built out. A second growth spurt multiplied the frames fivefold again. Beekeepers then split the frames evenly across four hive boxes, keeping only one box's frames in this story. That box's frames were then multiplied eightfold when the beekeeper added matching frames from a supply order, and a final seasonal buildup multiplied the count fourfold. How many frames were in that box by the end of the season?
